situation (example wording): "Carjackings in Texas in 2024" (a NIBRS-only crime or detail for a state or the nation) when some agencies reported only some months
what the app does today: State and national NIBRS figures are not built.
proposed behavior: Sum every month any agency reported, as the FBI does, with a clear disclaimer: how many agencies are counted, what share of the population they cover, and that agencies reporting only some months are included. A button shows only consistent reporters (agencies that reported every month of the period). Matches P03. Coverage note (coordinator decision, following Jeff's CDE-like coverage rule): the share is of the state's Crime Index population (the official estimate the state's rate answers use), not the sum of agency populations. The disclaimer states two figures: (1) the agencies included and the share of the state's population they cover, counting any agency that reported at least one month of the period; (2) how many of them reported every month, and their population share. No mean of monthly shares and no lowest-month figure. The nation is the 50 states and DC; territories and federal agencies are excluded, and the disclaimer says so.
exact default or choices offered: Default: every reported month, with the disclaimer. Button: "Show only agencies that reported every month". Coverage: agencies reporting any month and their share of the Crime Index population; agencies reporting every month and their share.
why: The FBI's own way of summing what was reported, with the gaps said plainly and the consistent view one click away.
status: Decided 2026-10-30 (Jeff: "I think it's b like the fbi does but with a clear disclaimer and button to select only consistent reporters"); coverage note 2026-10-30 (coordinator decision, following Jeff's CDE-like coverage rule, "coverage = CDE-like population_pct"; Jeff can override); the button's name is amended by P80
